My mum lived with dementia for 8 years. My adult son & I shared the responsibility. Even when nursing home care becomes inevitable your job is not done. You still have to supervise, advocate for them, negotiate with the care home as well as managing their financial affairs, sell the family home, keep accounts for the Office of the Public Guardian. But I never found the information hard to get & I don't think, for me, a support network would have helped. It wouldn't have stopped the heartbreak, or the exhaustion of coping with the demands alongside a full time job. It wouldn't have stopped me walking the beach in the rain so I could cry freely & the tears wouldn't show as I watched her decline. It wouldn't have stopped me having to sell my vintage (because I'm vintage) childhood teddy to help meet the care costs the government won't help with. The information & support is there already. It's the heartbreak & exhaustion that gets you.

Why did the art thief’s van run out of gas as he drove away from the museum? Because he had no Monet to buy Degas to make the Van Gogh.

A Vincent van Gogh painting has set a new record after selling for £145 million at a Sotheby's auction in New York. At its first appearance at auction, the painting Chataigniers en fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees) set the highest price a Van Gogh painting has sold for at auction and the second highest for any artwork sold at Sotheby's. Gustav Klimt's Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer holds that honour, sold a year ago at Sotheby's for 236.4 million (£180 million).

Blue Planet III has captured the moment dozens of fin whales work together, catching krill in a never-before-seen hunting strategy. Fin whales, the second-largest of all whale species, are normally solitary animals, rarely travelling in large groups or forming families. However, near Elephant Island, just off the coast of Antarctica, about 50 of the massive creatures came together for a coordinated hunt. In behaviour due to be recognised in a scientific journal, the whales formed a swirling ring of bodies, creating a pen around a dense ball of krill.
